protocols.title: Road Accident First Aid
protocols.description: General protocol for road traffic accident victims
steps: 🚨 ENSURE SAFETY: Check for oncoming traffic before approaching. Switch on hazard lights of nearby vehicles.
📞 CALL 112: Immediately call emergency services (112). State location, number of victims, visible injuries.
⚠️ DO NOT MOVE victim unless they are in immediate danger (fire/sinking vehicle). Spinal injuries may worsen.
🫁 CHECK BREATHING: Look, listen, feel for breathing for 10 seconds. If absent, begin CPR.
🩸 CONTROL BLEEDING: Apply firm, direct pressure using clean cloth. Do NOT remove embedded objects.
🧠 MONITOR CONSCIOUSNESS: Talk to the victim, keep them calm and awake. Note any loss of consciousness.
🌡️ PREVENT SHOCK: Lay victim flat (unless spinal injury suspected), elevate legs 30cm if no leg/spinal injury.
🚑 AWAIT AMBULANCE: Do not give food or water. Keep victim warm. Stay until help arrives.
warnings: ⚠️ Do NOT remove helmets unless airway is blocked — neck injuries are common
⚠️ Do NOT give pain medication without medical guidance
⚠️ Do NOT leave the victim alone

protocols.title: Cardiac Arrest / Heart Attack
protocols.description: Protocol for cardiac arrest and heart attack emergencies
steps: 📞 CALL 112 IMMEDIATELY: Cardiac emergencies are time-critical — every minute counts.
🫁 START CPR: Place heel of hand on centre of chest, push hard & fast (100-120 compressions/min, 5cm deep).
💨 GIVE RESCUE BREATHS: After 30 compressions, give 2 rescue breaths (tilt head, lift chin, seal mouth).
🔋 USE AED IF AVAILABLE: Turn on Automated External Defibrillator, follow voice prompts.
🔄 CONTINUE CPR: Do not stop until emergency services arrive or victim shows signs of life.
💊 ASPIRIN: If victim is conscious and not allergic, give 300mg aspirin to chew (not swallow whole).
🛋️ POSITION: Sit patient upright or in most comfortable position. Loosen tight clothing.
😌 KEEP CALM: Reduce patient's anxiety — stress worsens cardiac events.
warnings: ⚠️ Survival drops 10% per minute without CPR — start immediately
⚠️ Do NOT leave victim alone even for a moment
⚠️ Do NOT give food or water

protocols.title: Stroke Emergency
protocols.description: Protocol for suspected stroke — FAST protocol
steps: 🔍 USE FAST TEST: Face drooping? Arm weakness? Speech difficulty? Time to call 112!
📞 CALL 112 IMMEDIATELY: Note exact time symptoms started — critical for treatment decisions.
🛋️ POSITION: Lay victim on their side if unconscious or vomiting. Keep head slightly elevated.
⏱️ NOTE TIME: Record exactly when symptoms first appeared — determines treatment eligibility.
🚫 DO NOT give food, water, or medication — swallowing may be impaired.
🧊 DO NOT apply ice or heat to the affected area.
😌 KEEP CALM: Reassure victim, keep them still and comfortable.
🔄 MONITOR: Watch for breathing changes, loss of consciousness, or seizures until help arrives.
warnings: ⚠️ Stroke treatment window is 3-4.5 hours — get to hospital FAST
⚠️ Do NOT give aspirin for stroke (it can worsen bleeding strokes)
⚠️ Do NOT let the victim 'sleep it off'

protocols.title: Severe Bleeding Control
protocols.description: Protocol for controlling serious external bleeding
steps: 🧤 PROTECT YOURSELF: Use gloves or plastic bag if available to avoid blood-borne infections.
🤲 DIRECT PRESSURE: Place clean cloth or bandage firmly over wound. Press continuously for 10 minutes.
⏫ ELEVATE: If no fracture suspected, raise the injured limb above heart level.
🎗️ TOURNIQUET (Limb only): If bleeding is life-threatening from arm/leg, apply tourniquet 5cm above wound. Note time applied.
🚫 DO NOT remove the cloth if it soaks through — add more on top and keep pressing.
📞 CALL 112: All severe bleeding requires emergency medical attention.
🌡️ PREVENT SHOCK: Keep victim warm, lying down. Elevate legs if no spinal/leg injury.
💬 REASSURE: Keep victim calm — anxiety increases heart rate and blood loss.
warnings: ⚠️ Do NOT remove embedded objects from wounds
⚠️ Do NOT use tourniquet on neck, chest, or abdomen
⚠️ Never remove tourniquet once applied — only medical staff should do this

protocols.title: Bone Fracture First Aid
protocols.description: Protocol for suspected bone fractures and broken bones
steps: 🛑 IMMOBILIZE: Do NOT attempt to straighten the bone. Support it in the position found.
📏 SPLINT: Use rigid material (stick, rolled newspaper) padded with cloth. Extend splint beyond joints above and below fracture.
🧊 ICE: Apply ice pack (wrapped in cloth) to reduce swelling. Never apply ice directly to skin.
📞 CALL 112 if: Open fracture, spinal/hip/pelvis fracture, severe pain, significant deformity, or loss of sensation.
🩸 OPEN FRACTURE: Cover wound with clean dressing. Do NOT push bone back in.
⚡ CHECK CIRCULATION: Check pulse, sensation, and movement below the fracture site.
🔄 MONITOR: Watch for shock symptoms — pale, cold, clammy skin, rapid breathing.
🚫 DO NOT give food or water — surgery may be needed.
warnings: ⚠️ NEVER try to realign or straighten broken bone
⚠️ Suspected spinal fracture — do NOT move victim at all
⚠️ Open fractures carry high infection risk — keep wound covered

protocols.title: Burn Injury First Aid
protocols.description: Protocol for thermal, chemical, and electrical burns
steps: 🔥 REMOVE HEAT SOURCE: Stop the burning process — remove from fire, chemical contact, or electrical source.
💧 COOL THE BURN: Run cool (not cold/ice) water over burn for 20 FULL MINUTES. Do NOT use ice.
📞 CALL 112: For burns larger than palm size, burns to face/hands/genitals/joints, or all chemical/electrical burns.
🚫 DO NOT: Apply butter, toothpaste, oil, or home remedies. Do NOT burst blisters.
🎁 COVER: Loosely cover with clean non-fluffy material (cling film or clean plastic bag). Do NOT wrap tightly.
💊 PAIN RELIEF: Paracetamol or ibuprofen can be given if victim is conscious and has no allergies.
🌡️ PREVENT SHOCK: Keep victim warm except for burned area. Lay down, elevate legs.
💧 HYDRATION: If conscious and minor burn, encourage small sips of water.
warnings: ⚠️ NEVER use ice — it causes further tissue damage
⚠️ Chemical burns — brush off dry chemicals before water irrigation
⚠️ Electrical burns — ensure power source is OFF before touching victim

protocols.title: Drowning Emergency
protocols.description: Protocol for near-drowning and water rescue
steps: 🆘 CALL FOR HELP: Call 112 immediately. Do NOT enter water unless trained.
🪢 REACH OR THROW: Use rope, stick, or flotation device to reach victim. Do NOT swim to victim unless trained.
🏖️ REMOVAL: Remove victim from water. Be careful of potential spinal injury if they fell/dived.
🫁 CHECK BREATHING: Tilt head back, lift chin, check for 10 seconds. Begin CPR if not breathing.
🔁 CPR: 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths. Do NOT stop.
👤 RECOVERY POSITION: If breathing, place in recovery position (on their side).
🌡️ HYPOTHERMIA: Remove wet clothing, cover with blankets. Hypothermia is a risk even in warm weather.
🏥 HOSPITAL: All drowning victims need medical evaluation even if they seem recovered.
warnings: ⚠️ Secondary drowning can occur hours later — always get medical evaluation
⚠️ Victim may vomit during CPR — turn head to side briefly
⚠️ Do NOT hold victim upside down to remove water

protocols.title: Head Injury First Aid
protocols.description: Protocol for traumatic brain injury and head wounds
steps: 📞 CALL 112: All head injuries should be evaluated by medical professionals.
🛑 IMMOBILIZE HEAD & NECK: Keep victim still. Support head in position found if spinal injury suspected.
🩸 CONTROL BLEEDING: Apply firm pressure around (not on) skull wounds. Use clean cloth.
👁️ MONITOR CONSCIOUSNESS: Use AVPU scale — Alert, Voice response, Pain response, Unresponsive.
🔍 WATCH FOR DANGER SIGNS: Repeated vomiting, seizures, unequal pupils, increasing headache, confusion.
🚫 DO NOT: Give pain medication (masks symptoms), give food/water, leave alone.
👤 RECOVERY POSITION: Only if victim is unconscious and breathing with no spinal injury suspected.
💬 KEEP AWAKE: Talk to victim, but do NOT let them sleep until medically assessed.
warnings: ⚠️ Intracranial bleeding can develop slowly — symptoms worsen over hours
⚠️ NEVER remove helmet if neck/spinal injury suspected
⚠️ Confusion, amnesia, or loss of consciousness = serious injury regardless of appearance
